questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracketed terms** first and then group **positive** and **negative** values.

Expression → 82 + 66 − 70 + 73 − 54 + 36

Sum of positive values → 82 + 66 + 73 + 36 = 257

Sum of negative values → 70 + 54 = 124

Final Result → 257 − 124 = 133

**∴ The correct answer is 133.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 82 + 66 − (41 + 29) + 73 − 54 + 36

**Method Used:** Apply the **BODMAS rule** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 82 + 66 − (70) + 73 − 54 + 36

⇒ 148 − 70 + 73 − 54 + 36

⇒ 78 + 73 − 54 + 36

⇒ 151 − 54 + 36

⇒ 97 + 36

⇒ 133

**∴ The correct answer is 133.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **Brackets** first, then **Of** (powers/roots), then **Division** and **Multiplication**, and finally **Addition** and **Subtraction**.

Grouping Method

In multi-step **addition** and **subtraction**, it is often faster and more accurate to sum all positive terms and negative terms separately before the final subtraction.

Sign Convention

When a **negative sign** precedes a bracket, the signs of all terms inside the bracket are reversed when the bracket is opened: −(a + b) = −a − b.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using **BODMAS**: 93 − 48 + 44 + 37 − 19 + 16

Sum of **positive** numbers: 93 + 44 + 37 + 16 = 190

Sum of **negative** numbers: 48 + 19 = 67

Final difference: 190 − 67 = 123

**∴ The correct answer is 123.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 93 − 48 + 22 × 2 + (37 ÷ 1) − 19 + 16

**Method:** Apply **BODMAS** rule sequentially.

⇒ 93 − 48 + 22 × 2 + 37 − 19 + 16 (Solving **Bracket** and **Division**: 37 ÷ 1 = 37)

⇒ 93 − 48 + 44 + 37 − 19 + 16 (Solving **Multiplication**: 22 × 2 = 44)

⇒ (93 + 44 + 37 + 16) − (48 + 19) (Grouping **Addition** and **Subtraction** terms)

⇒ 190 − 67 = 123

**∴ The correct answer is 123.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

It represents the order: **Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**. It is essential for solving complex arithmetic expressions.

Grouping Method

To minimize errors in long **Addition/Subtraction** strings, group all positive terms and negative terms separately before the final subtraction.

questions.question: (15.3 + 5.3)² - 4 × 15.3 × 5.3 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity: **(a + b)² − 4ab = (a − b)²**

Identify the values: **a = 15.3** and **b = 5.3**.

Required result = (15.3 − 5.3)²

Required result = (10)² = **100**

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (15.3 + 5.3)² − 4 × 15.3 × 5.3

**Formula Used:**

Standard expansion: **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** or **direct calculation**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ (20.6)² − 4 × 15.3 × 5.3

⇒ 424.36 − 4 × 81.09

⇒ 424.36 − 324.36

⇒ 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binomial Squared Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². These are the foundations for complex simplification.

Relationship between Sum and Difference

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. This identity is extremely useful in **Quantitative Aptitude** to find the product when sum and difference are given.

Sum of Squares Formula

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This relates the squares of the sum and difference to the sum of the individual squares.

questions.question: The side of a square is 8 cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **perimeter** of a square is the **total boundary length**, which is 4 **times** its side.

Given **side** = 8 cm.

Perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the **square** (s) = 8 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/187395fa7ed7054e2bca9d0022ef3acca10d854717d04723192e8c65e43fb1d2.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of Square = **Sum of all sides** = 4 × **side**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × s

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 8 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

The total space occupied by the square is given by the formula: **Area = side²**.

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the line connecting opposite vertices is: **Diagonal = side × √2**.

Properties of a Square

A square is a **regular quadrilateral** where all four sides are equal and all four angles are **90°**.

questions.question: The area of a rhombus is 84 square cm. One of the diagonal is 14 cm. What is the ratio of the two diagonals?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Area** of **rhombus** = (d₁ × d₂) / 2 84 = (14 × d₂) / 2 84 = 7 × d₂ ⇒ d₂ = 12 cm Required **ratio** (d₁ : d₂) = 14 : 12 = 7 : 6 **∴ The correct answer is 7 : 6.**

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 60 cm. One of the diagonal is 18 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of both the diagonals of the rhombus?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Side of **Rhombus** (a) = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Semi-diagonals (d₁/2, d₂/2) and side (a) form a **Pythagorean Triplet**. Semi-diagonal 1 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm. Using triplet (9, 12, 15): Semi-diagonal 2 = 12 cm. Second **Diagonal** (d₂) = 12 × 2 = 24 cm. Sum = 18 + 24 = 42 cm. **∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

questions.question: Average age of a group of 16 boys is 20 years. Two boys with ages 18 years and 19 years left the group. One boy with age 32 years joined the group. What is the new average age (in years) of the group?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Net change in the sum of ages = Age of **joining boy** − Sum of ages of **leaving boys** Net change = 32 − (18 + 19) = 32 − 37 = −5 years New group size = 16 − 2 + 1 = **15 boys** New Average = (Initial Total Sum + Net Change) ÷ New Count = (16 × 20 − 5) ÷ 15 = 21 years **∴ The correct answer is 21 years.**

questions.question: A = 2⁵ x 3², B = 2⁸ x 3⁴. What is the product of Highest Common Factor and Least Common Multiple of A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Property: **Product of HCF and LCM** of two numbers is equal to the **Product of the numbers** (A × B).

Required Product = (2⁵ × 3²) × (2⁸ × 3⁴)

Using **law of exponents** am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ, we add the powers of the same bases.

Product = 2⁽⁵⁺⁸⁾ × 3⁽²⁺⁴⁾ = 2¹³ × 3⁶

**∴ The correct answer is 2¹³ × 3⁶.**

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple of all prime numbers between 5 and 12?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **prime numbers** strictly between 5 and 12 are **7** and **11**. For any set of **prime numbers**, the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is always their **product** because they have no common factors other than 1. LCM = 7 × 11 = 77. **∴ The correct answer is 77.**

questions.question: If A = 8X and B = 6X, then B is what percent of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Determine the **ratio** of **B** to **A** directly by cancelling common terms.

**B : A** = 6X : 8X = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4

Required percentage = (3 ÷ 4) × 100

Since 3/4 is equivalent to **75%** in standard fraction-to-percentage conversion.

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Value of **A** = 8X

Value of **B** = 6X

**Formula Used:**

Required Percentage = (Value to be compared ÷ Base Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f15e1839a2700bde54095fccbca7710328e5fa34eab96c3bfa8fe4fd5c22d9f8.png] 

⇒ Required Percentage = (**B** ÷ **A**) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (6X ÷ 8X) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (6 ÷ 8) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (3 ÷ 4) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 0.75 × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions like 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, 3/4 = 75%, and 1/5 = 20% are essential for quick calculations in competitive exams.

Base of Comparison

In the phrase 'X is what percent of Y', the value following 'of' (which is **Y**) is always taken as the **denominator** (base).

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Increase or Decrease = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. In this case, B is 25% less than A.

questions.question: Selling price and cost price of an article is Rs. 6000 and Rs. 8000 respectively. What is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 8000 : 6000 = 4 : 3.

Loss in units = 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = ₹8000

**Selling Price (SP)** of the article = ₹6000

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e969283eb30b7a3245fa18477beb56b891f2e68e0ec3382ce4ec9551cb830a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = 8000 − 6000

⇒ Loss = ₹2000

⇒ Loss % = (2000 ÷ 8000) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

When SP is greater than CP, Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Selling Price Calculation

If loss percentage is given, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Cost Price Calculation

If profit percentage is given, CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: 25 percent of the cost price of an article is equal to the 10 percent of its selling price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** is the inverse of the given percentage values.

CP : SP = 10 : 25 = 2 : 5

**Profit** = 5 − 2 = 3 units

**Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (3 ÷ 2) × 100 = 150%

**∴ The correct answer is 150%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

25% of **Cost Price (CP)** = 10% of **Selling Price (SP)**

**Formula Used:**

**Profit %** = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bbbb9649f96df9ca83a6e8f94f41d6748625259bde9b080dfc7edc45431e5104.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 ÷ 100) × CP = (10 ÷ 100) × SP

⇒ 25 × CP = 10 × SP

⇒ CP ÷ SP = 10 ÷ 25

⇒ CP ÷ SP = 2 ÷ 5

⇒ Let **Cost Price** = 2 units and **Selling Price** = 5 units

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 5 − 2 = 3 units

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 2) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 1.5 × 100 = 150%

**∴ The correct answer is 150%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Profit and Loss

Profit occurs when SP > CP. **Profit** = SP − CP. **Loss** occurs when CP > SP. **Loss** = CP − SP.

Selling Price Formula

When profit percentage is known: **SP** = CP × (100 + Profit %) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: What should be subtracted from 420 so that the number obtained will become equal to 180 percent of 120?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **target value**: 180% of 120 = 1.8 × 120 = 216

The number to be **subtracted** from 420 to get 216 is the **difference**.

Required Number = 420 − 216 = 204

**∴ The correct answer is 204.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number = **420**

Target value = **180% of 120**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b9642239538b7a4763e1c0daa75687e21f5a870c4f54211c6fbc727895d396d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number to be **subtracted** be **x**.

⇒ According to the question:

⇒ 420 − x = 180% × 120

⇒ 420 − x = (180 ÷ 100) × 120

⇒ 420 − x = 1.8 × 120

⇒ 420 − x = 216

⇒ x = 420 − 216

⇒ x = 204

**∴ The correct answer is 204.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find **x% of y**, use the formula: **(x × y) ÷ 100**. This represents a portion of the whole value.

Converting Percentage to Decimal

Divide the percentage by 100 to get the decimal equivalent. For example, **180% = 1.80**.

Word Problem Translation

Terms like **of** usually imply multiplication, while **subtracted from** indicates the order: **Base − Value**.

questions.question: R did 4/7 part of a work on first day. He did 2/5 part of the remaining work on second day. Now the remaining work is 18 units. What is the total work (in units)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining fraction after first day = 1 − 4/7 = 3/7

Remaining fraction after second day = 3/7 × (1 − 2/5) = 3/7 × 3/5 = 9/35

According to the question, 9/35 units = 18

Total work (1 unit) = 18 × 35 ÷ 9 = 70 units

**∴ The correct answer is 70 units.**

questions.question: A and B are employed in a work. A worked for 2 days and B worked for 6 days. Per day work of A and B is 5 units and 2 units respectively. A and B received total wages of Rs. 2750. What is the difference between shares (in Rs.) of A and B?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of work done (**A : B**) = (2 × 5) : (6 × 2) = 10 : 12 = **5 : 6** Total wage ratio parts = 5 + 6 = 11 parts Value of 11 parts = **₹2750** Difference between shares (A and B) = 6 − 5 = 1 part Value of 1 part = 2750 ÷ 11 = 250 **∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. Length of each train is 238 metres. They cross each other in 14 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

Since speeds are equal (v), Relative Speed = v + v = **2v**.

Total distance to cross each other = Sum of lengths = 238 + 238 = **476 m**.

Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Time ⇒ 2v = 476 ÷ 14 = **34 m/s**.

Speed of each train (v) = 34 ÷ 2 = **17 m/s**.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = **238 m**

Length of second train (L₂) = **238 m**

Time taken (t) = **14 seconds**

Let the speed of each train be **v m/s**.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

v₁ + v₂ = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/392f398b7efcfe34d1fbbd64859c96bc255f0b7543c1045a73fd9a1560cedf39.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 238 + 238 = **476 m**

⇒ Relative Speed = v + v = **2v**

⇒ 2v = 476 ÷ 14

⇒ 2v = 34

⇒ v = 34 ÷ 2

⇒ v = **17 m/s**

**∴ The correct answer is 17 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **same direction**, relative speed = |v₁ − v₂|. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = v₁ + v₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a stationary object of length Lₚ (like a platform), the total distance covered is **Length of Train + Lₚ**.

questions.question: A man covers 1/3 part of a distance at the speed of 40 km/hr. He covers the remaining distance at the speed of 50 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for this journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume total **distance** as LCM of **speeds** (40, 50) × **denominator** (3) = 200 × 3 = 600 km.

1/3rd **distance** (200 km) at 40 km/hr → **Time₁** = 200 ÷ 40 = 5 hrs.

Remaining **distance** (400 km) at 50 km/hr → **Time₂** = 400 ÷ 50 = 8 hrs.

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 600 ÷ (5 + 8) = 600/13 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 600/13 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Part 1 speed (v₁) = 40 km/hr, Part 2 speed (v₂) = 50 km/hr, Part 1 distance = 1/3 of total, Part 2 distance = 2/3 of total.

**Formula:** **Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e1f76d2ce7d479c05b537931199419ac38144f023c198c5f77d9ddba228a192.png] 

⇒ Let the total **distance** be **d** km.

⇒ **Time₁** = (d/3) ÷ 40 = d ÷ 120 hrs

⇒ **Time₂** = (2d/3) ÷ 50 = 2d ÷ 150 = d ÷ 75 hrs

⇒ Total Time = (d ÷ 120) + (d ÷ 75)

⇒ LCM of 120 and 75 is 600. Total Time = (5d + 8d) ÷ 600 = 13d ÷ 600 hrs

⇒ **Average Speed** = d ÷ (13d/600) = (d × 600) ÷ 13d = 600/13 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 600/13 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When two equal distances are covered at speeds **x** and **y**, the **Average Speed** is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Harmonic Mean of Speeds

**Average Speed** is always the harmonic mean of the individual speeds when the distances covered are equal.

Weighted Average Speed Formula

For different distances d₁, d₂, ... and speeds v₁, v₂, ..., the **Average Speed** = (d₁ + d₂ + ...) ÷ (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂ + ...).

questions.question: The marked price of an article is (8/3) of the cost price. Its selling price is (5/8) of the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** = 3 : 8

Ratio of **Marked Price (MP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 8 : 5

Combined ratio **CP : MP : SP** = 3 : 8 : 5

**Profit** = **SP − CP** = 5 − 3 = 2 units

**Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (2 ÷ 3) × 100 = 200/3 %

**∴ The correct answer is (200/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = (8/3) × **Cost Price (CP)**

**Selling Price (SP)** = (5/8) × **Marked Price (MP)**

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [(**Selling Price** − **Cost Price**) ÷ **Cost Price**] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4849c591523708804bea3f48664f66267eadc67bde42e776e5ae4363ee8b8af0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = x

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = (8/3) × x = 8x/3

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = (5/8) × (8x/3)

⇒ **SP** = 5x/3

⇒ **Profit** = **SP** − **CP** = (5x/3) − x = 2x/3

⇒ **Profit %** = [(2x/3) ÷ x] × 100

⇒ **Profit %** = (2/3) × 100 = 200/3 %

**∴ The correct answer is (200/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on an article or the label price is called the **Marked Price**. **Discount** is always calculated on the **MP**.

Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of **MP** to **CP** can be expressed as MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Selling Price (SP)

**Selling Price** is the final price after applying a discount to the **Marked Price** (SP = MP − Discount).

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 6000. It is sold at a discount of 30 percent. The profit percentage is 50 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **CP-MP Ratio** formula: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**

CP / 6000 = (100 − 30) / (100 + 50) = 70 / 150 = 7 / 15

CP = (7 / 15) × 6000 = 7 × 400 = ₹2800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹6000, **Discount** = 30%, **Profit** = 50%

**Formula:** **Selling Price (SP)** = MP × (100 − D%)/100 | **Cost Price (CP)** = SP × 100/(100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/614be95c7957175dda0a67d3bda694f835be5e289f8a665865b8e0bc93f2bf40.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 6000 − 30% of 6000

⇒ SP = 6000 − (30/100) × 6000 = 6000 − 1800 = ₹4200

⇒ **Profit** is 50%, so SP = 150% of CP

⇒ 4200 = CP × (150/100)

⇒ CP = 4200 × (2/3)

⇒ CP = 1400 × 2 = ₹2800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%) is the most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit.

Successive Discounts

Equivalent discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = (a + b − ab/100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(Marked Price − Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100.
